en: The Sutra on the Bodhisattva’s Rejection of the Dharma of Desire for Form, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Later Qin.
Regarding female form: it is a worldly shackle; ordinary people are attached to it and cannot extricate themselves. As for women...
Form (*rūpa*) is a grave affliction of the world; ordinary persons are constrained by it, unable to escape it even unto death.
Female form (*strī-rūpa*) is a calamity of decay in the world; when ordinary persons encounter it, no misfortune fails to befall them.
Once the practitioner has attained equanimity, if they should again look back with longing, it is like having escaped from prison yet thinking of re-entering;
like having recovered from madness yet delighting in it;
or like having been cured of an illness yet wishing to fall ill again.
The wise man is angered by this, knowing that such a person is mad and will stumble and fall, with no day remaining for his life!
Ordinary people cherish beauty and willingly become its servants, galloping about for it their entire lives and undergoing toil and hardship for its sake.

Even if one were to be executed by the axe or the stake, or cut into pieces inch by inch, or if spears and arrows were to rain down upon them, they would accept it with a willing heart and not regard it as a calamity.
This is no more than a madman delighting in madness.

If a practitioner can cast it aside and disregard it, they will break their shackles and shed their chains; freed from the madness of evil and the disease of aversion, they will be liberated from decline and calamity. Thus secure and auspicious, they shall emerge from the prison and forever be free from suffering and hardship.
The characteristics of women are such that their speech is like honey while their hearts are like poison; it is, for example,
like a deep, clear pool or a polished mirror inhabited by a dragon,
or a golden mountain and precious cave occupied by a lion.
One should know that this harm is not to be approached:
domestic discord arises from women;
the destruction of clans and the ruin of lineages are the crimes of women.
It is truly a hidden thief that extinguishes a person’s wisdom and clarity;
it is also like a hunting enclosure, from which few can escape.
It is like a high net into which flocks of birds fall, unable to struggle free and fly away.
Furthermore, it is like a dense net into which many fish cast themselves, only to have their entrails cut out and their flesh served on the carving board;
it is also like a dark pit into which those without eyes throw themselves, like moths rushing into a flame.
Therefore, the wise know this and distance themselves from it, so as not to suffer its harm;
they loathe and detest it, and are not deluded by such things.
*The Sutra on the Bodhisattva’s Rebuke of the Dharma of Desire for Form*.
